root.name: Slav Defense: Alekhine Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. e3

overview: White plays 5.e3 intending to regain c4 with Bxc4, and Black responds 5...b5 6.a4 b4 to hold the pawn, chasing the knight from c3. After 7.Na2 or 7.Nb1 White has lost time but builds the centre with Bxc4 and e4 or Nxb4 ideas, while Black's extra queenside space may become a target. Theory is heavy and the play is double-edged.

white_ideas.idea: Win back the c4 pawn with Bxc4 after Na2 and aim for a central break with e4.
Target the b4 pawn and the weakened queenside.

black_ideas.idea: Hold the extra pawn with ...b5 and ...b4 and trade off White's pieces.
Develop with ...Ba6 or ...Bb7 and ...e6 and break with ...c5.

typical_structures.structure: Black advanced b-pawn on b4 with c4 pawn lost or held; White central pawns d4 and e3.

character.notes: Black's queenside pawn pushes and White's central break give mutual risks; double-edged and theory heavy.

gambit.notes: The c4 pawn is regained with Bxc4 in the usual lines; counted as accepted rather than a gambit.

soundness.notes: Sound for both sides; a respected main branch of the Slav.

structure.notes: Slav structure with a half-open c-file and a central pawn exchange.

level.notes: Requires knowing the specific move orders after 5...b5.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5...b5 6.a4 b4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. e3 b5 6. a4 b4
sublines_that_differ.how: The sharper main line, with Black holding the pawn.

character.reason: Black's b-pawn pushes against White's central play make it double-edged.

gambit.reason: The pawn on c4 comes back by force in the usual lines.

soundness.reason: A standard main-line branch of the Slav.

structure.reason: Slav structure with a half-open c-file.

level.reason: Needs knowledge of specific lines but not very deep.

plans.reason: Black advances b5-b4 to hold c4.
